1.0.0.en: Achaia: the southern region of Greece. The Romans made Corinth the capital of Achaia.

1.0.1.en: St. Paul the Apostle begins by mentioning his name, to confirm that he is the writer of the epistle, together with his disciple Timothy, who had visited Corinth. He declares that God chose him as His apostle, to please Him and to do His will.

1.1.0.en: He sends them grace and peace. God is the source of grace, for He has graciously granted us salvation. This also shows the oneness of the Father with the Son as one source of grace and peace.

1.1.1.en: The Church took up this prayer and made it a blessing for the people at their dismissal, so the priest says, "The love of God the Father, the grace of His only-begotten Son, and the communion and gift and operation of the Holy Spirit be with you."

1.1.2.en: Every Christian has a mission that he received from God on the day of his baptism, which is the salvation of his soul and witness to Christ in the world, and every grace in his life has God as its source. So thank God every day for the grace He gives you, and try to invest these graces so that you may enjoy them, and your fellowship with God will increase.

1.2.s.en: (2) God is the source of comfort

1.2.0.en: The Father of our Lord Jesus Christ: the hypostasis of the Father.

1.2.1.en: The Father of mercies: the source of all compassion, mercy and tenderness.

1.2.2.en: The God of all comfort: the wellspring of comfort and support for all people.

1.2.3.en: Paul affirms that there is no mercy, compassion or comfort apart from God, because He is the source and father of all mercy and comfort.

1.3.0.en: Comforts us: supports us, makes us feel His presence with us, and gladdens our hearts.

1.3.1.en: God is the source of all comfort, and He is the One who comforted the Apostles and the saints in all their afflictions and trials. All the Apostles experienced this comfort, because they were exposed to many sufferings and the Lord was with them and comforted them. Comfort is not only, at times, the prevention of affliction, but God's support of us in it, so that it does not harm us. This made the suffering Apostles and saints able to comfort those in distress as well and to lighten their pains.

1.4.0.en: The Apostle encourages the Corinthians to face the afflictions they meet, telling them that as afflictions and sufferings increase, God's grace to them will increase, so that they will experience His work in them and feel His presence with them. This is the greatest thing in existence, indeed it is a pledge of the Kingdom.

1.5.0.en: Your salvation, which is effective: that is, the grace of Christ working in the one who believes, so that he may endure sufferings and remain firm in the faith.

1.5.1.en: St. Paul declares that he and his fellow servants endure labors and afflictions for the sake of the preaching, so that the Corinthians may obtain salvation through Christ. The believers in Corinth, at the same time, endure sufferings because of their adherence to the faith.

1.5.2.en: And if the Apostle and the servants receive comforts from God in their service, they make those they serve share in them as well, for they tell them of God's work in the ministry, so that they are comforted and rejoice with the Apostles.

1.6.0.en: The Apostle affirms his confidence and hope concerning the believers in the Church of Corinth: if they endure sufferings, they will also receive comforts and support from God.

1.6.1.en: May we feel that every pain and affliction in our life is a sharing in the sufferings of Christ, and Christ Himself, who suffered for us, will not leave us, but will comfort us and strengthen us. As great as our suffering and weariness, so great will be our joys and God's support of us.

1.7.s.en: (3) Paul as an example in enduring afflictions

1.7.0.en: Asia: not the continent of Asia, but the western part of Asia Minor, which is present-day Turkey.

1.7.1.en: Paul presents himself as an example by what happened to him of afflictions in Asia. These afflictions made Paul feel discouraged and despairing of escaping with his life from death.

1.8.0.en: The afflictions and dangers to which Paul was exposed were expected to end in his death. Therefore, having lost every human strength and thought of deliverance, he had no recourse but to trust in God, who is able to raise him from the dead even if he died.

1.9.0.en: God delivered Paul from the sentence of death, and He will deliver him again from all dangers, because God does not change; He is the same yesterday, today and forever (Heb 13:8). God delivers His children at all times, and then the affliction becomes a spiritual experience that supports a person when he is exposed to afflictions in the future.

1.10.0.en: By many persons... through many: the believers in Corinth and the other churches who pray for Paul and his companions.

1.10.1.en: The Corinthians gave Paul help, which was prayer on his behalf, that the Lord might deliver him from all afflictions. Therefore God granted him deliverance and strength to endure sufferings, and this led them to give thanks to God.

1.10.2.en: If you live as a stranger to the world and are occupied with preparing for eternal life, your being affected will be limited and bearable when afflictions meet you. So control your desires and do not cling to material things, so that you may grow in your relationship with God and thus endure the afflictions of life.

1.11.0.en: St. Paul declares that his actions are in simplicity, relying on the grace of God and not on human wisdom. He had wanted to go to them from Ephesus, but for many reasons he changed his mind, and some doubted him, thinking he was not wise. So he explained to them that he does not act by his own thoughts, but in simplicity submits to the Holy Spirit, and God guides him.

1.12.0.en: Other things: we do not mean anything else, hidden and different from what is plain in our words.

1.12.1.en: What you read or acknowledge: what you understood from our words, because our words are frank and clear.

1.12.2.en: You shall acknowledge to the end: Paul makes clear that whoever does not know him well and doubts him will know him afterward and trust him.

1.12.3.en: In part: some believers did not know Paul fully and trust him completely, so their knowledge of him was partial and would be completed with the passing of time.

1.12.4.en: The Apostle shows that his words are frank and he means nothing but what he wrote. Some thought he wrote words by which he meant something else. But he affirms that his words are simple, frank and clear.

1.12.5.en: Some of the believers in Corinth had known Paul and trusted him, while others did not yet trust him. So he tells them that in the end they will know him as their apostle who is clear in his words to them. And when Christ comes in His Second Coming, the believers in Corinth will boast in being Paul's children, just as he will boast in being their father.

1.13.0.en: Paul's confidence in his fatherhood to them, and their holding fast to their sonship to him, made him plan to come from Ephesus to Corinth, then go to Macedonia and return to them to visit them a second time and confirm their faith, on his way back from Macedonia to Jerusalem and Judea.

1.14.0.en: I was minded to come: that is, to visit Corinth before reaching Macedonia.

1.14.1.en: Lightness: haste and impulsiveness in thinking.

1.14.2.en: According to the flesh: human purposes, and not the guidance of the Holy Spirit.

1.14.3.en: Yea yea... nay nay: I declare truths and then draw back from them and say the opposite.

1.14.4.en: St. Paul asks in protest about what had happened: he first thought of going from Ephesus to Corinth and then Macedonia, then changed his mind and went directly to Macedonia. He asks whether his first plan was made with human haste or had a personal purpose. The answer, of course, is no, because he moves by the guidance of the Holy Spirit. His thought was to visit Corinth, but God guided him to go to Macedonia first and then return to Corinth. His enemies thought that he was speaking contradictory words, announcing that he would visit Corinth and then retracting his word and not visiting it, so that they concluded from this that all his preaching was doubtful, and what he said about Christ could be retracted and changed.

1.15.0.en: God is true: God is witness to what I say, as a confirmation and assurance of the truth of his words. Our word toward you: the preaching of Christ.

1.15.1.en: Paul affirms that his word is true, and God is witness to this, that his preaching to them was truthful, and that he did not say anything he could retract or change.

1.16.1.en: Was not yea and nay: it is not possible to change or retract any truth they heard about Christ in the preaching to them.

1.16.2.en: In Him is yea: that is, a firm truth that does not change, namely the truths of the preaching of Christ.

1.16.3.en: The Apostle affirms that the eternal Christ, in whom there is no change at all, whom Paul and his companions preached in Corinth, is true and firm, and it is not possible to change any truth they heard about Him.

1.17.0.en: The yea... and the Amen: the fulfillment of all the divine promises, because they are true.

1.17.1.en: By us: these divine promises were preached by Paul and his companions.

1.17.2.en: However great God's promises are, such as the acceptance of sinners and their justification and the support of His children in the hardest afflictions, all of this is true and will be accomplished so that God may be glorified in those who believe in Him.

1.18.0.en: Anointed us: the anointing with the Myron that takes place after Baptism.

1.18.1.en: God: that is, the Holy Spirit.

1.18.2.en: Sealed us: the sign of the cross made with the oil on all the members of the person is a divine seal declaring that these members have become God's possession, working for Him.

1.18.3.en: The source of our spiritual steadfastness is God, through our anointing with the Holy Spirit in the Sacrament of Myron, which is therefore called the Sacrament of Confirmation, and the Holy Spirit gives us the knowledge of God as a pledge of the perfect knowledge in eternity.

1.19.0.en: I call God for a record upon my soul: confirmation of the truth of what I say.

1.19.1.en: Not that we have dominion over your faith: that is, we do not want to control you.

1.19.2.en: Helpers of your joy: supporting you and confirming your faith so that you may rejoice with true joy. By faith ye stand: true faith is what establishes a person in Christ so that he rejoices. Paul explains truthfully before God a fact, which is that he did not come to Corinth in order to spare the believers there, because he would be compelled to rebuke them for their sins. This is not domination over them, but he wishes to support them on the way of their salvation and to rejoice in their joy with Christ.

1.19.3.en: Do you accept the guidance and rebukes of the Fathers and spiritual guides so that you repent and correct your mistakes?

1.19.4.en: And know that this is the way of your steadfastness in the spiritual life, and when you accept guidance you live a life of repentance, stand firm in the faith, and rejoice with true joy.

1.19.5.en: The Church's discipline of the sinner and thanking God for His work

2.0.s.en: (1) The reasons for Paul's not coming to Corinth

2.0.1.en: In heaviness: I grieve over your clinging to sin and rebuke you for your sins, and you grieve.

2.0.2.en: Who is he then that maketh me glad: Paul rejoices in their repentance and grieves over their lack of repentance, so he wishes to come to them after they repent through this epistle, and so rejoice in them.

2.0.3.en: This same: that is, what is written in the two preceding verses.

2.0.4.en: Paul decided not to visit Corinth because of their falling into many sins, and he would be compelled to rebuke them and they would grieve, and he did not want to grieve them. So he postponed the visit and sent this epistle, in which he calls them to repentance, so that when he visits them he may rejoice in their repentance, because the source of his joy is the repentance and joy of his children. How then could he grieve them with severe rebuke?!

2.0.5.en: Paul trusts in their love of God, so when they find him joyful at his visit to them, they will rejoice too, because love is strong between them and him.

2.0.6.en: The Second Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

2.1.0.en: When Paul learned of their sins, he grieved over them and wrote them this epistle with tears flowing for them, seeking their repentance. By this the Corinthians come to know the extent of his fatherhood and his love for sinners, especially the Corinthians. So they should not be upset by his rebuke, but feel his love and hasten to repentance.

2.1.1.en: My brother, when you speak to others, may you feel their feelings and not condemn them, but let your true aim in every word to them be love. True love makes us warn, guide, and sometimes rebuke those we love, but with love, gentleness and a spirit of meekness.

2.2.0.en: If any... such a one: he means the sinner in Corinth who was mentioned in the first epistle, who committed fornication with his father's wife, and Paul excommunicated him from the Church for a period so that he might repent (1 Cor 5:1). This sinner grieved not only the Apostle Paul, but the whole Church, because all are one body. So that Paul might not make the punishment on him heavier than this, he asked the Church, that is, the priests, to lift the excommunication from him and to restore him to partaking of the Holy Mysteries after he had spent the period of punishment and repentance.

2.3.1.en: Confirm your love toward him: show your love and your concern for him.

2.3.2.en: Paul asked them to forgive him, encourage him and show their love for him, so that despair would not overcome him.

2.4.0.en: The proof of you: your virtues and distinction as children of Paul, which appear in their obedience to him. Paul makes clear that their response to this word of his will show the extent of their obedience, and he affirms that they are his true children. That is, he asks for their obedience to him in forgiving this offender.

2.5.0.en: In the person of Christ: Paul feels that he is gathered with the believers in Corinth in the Church, and Christ is in their midst, so they are able to decide on the return of this sinner.

2.5.1.en: Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: lest he seize an opportunity and take any soul on the way of evil.

2.5.2.en: His devices: his attempts to make human beings fall.

2.5.3.en: Paul also declares that he forgave this sinner for the sake of his love for them, and consequently he loves this sinner, since he is one of his children. For he does not want any of them to remain in sin, whether by persisting in it if he is not punished, or, if the punishment is increased, by falling into despair of the possibility of repentance. By this we prevent the devil, who wants to make us fall into sin in any form, from prevailing.

2.5.4.en: We always pray in our prayers that God forgive us our trespasses, as we also forgive those who trespass against us. May we make peace with people and forgive them as God forgives us and pardons our mistakes. May we also forget people's weaknesses and not recall them to them, because the Lord says to us, "I will remember their sin no more" (Jer 31:34).

2.6.s.en: (3) Why did Paul not stay in Troas?

2.6.0.en: Paul went from Ephesus to Troas to preach Christ. There a new door for preaching was opened to him, to cross over to the region of Macedonia, which is northern Greece.

2.6.1.en: The Second Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

2.7.0.en: My brother: it is humility on Paul's part to call his son Titus "his brother."

2.7.1.en: Here Paul's feelings and humility appear, as he felt the lack of his son Titus, who was not with him, but this did not hinder him from continuing to preach, so he went from Troas to preach in the region of Macedonia.

2.7.2.en: It is good to be bound by feelings of love to those around you, so that you rejoice in their presence and miss them if they leave you. But do not be hindered from completing your worship or your service or your work if one of your loved ones leaves you, but lean on God, the source of love and help, and continue your life with zeal and strength.

2.8.s.en: (4) Thanksgiving to God for the success of the Gospel

2.8.0.en: Triumph: Paul feels that he walks with the servants and the believers in the Church as a company triumphing, with Christ as their leader, over the devil.

2.8.1.en: Paul thanks God, who made him a servant and a preacher in His name, so that he triumphs over the devil and gathers the souls that were under his grip and draws them to faith. By this Christ appears in Paul's life and in his preaching like a sweet fragrance that spreads quickly among those to whom he preaches in every place where he preached.

2.9.0.en: St. Paul declares that his preaching makes the hearers know Christ the Savior and spreads among them like a sweet fragrance, whether those who receive the word of life and so obtain salvation and new life, or those who reject it, so that the words of preaching condemn them and become a judgment against them on the Day of Judgment and lead them to eternal death.

2.9.1.en: Then he asks concerning the greatness of the ministry of preaching, saying, who is able to perform this ministry? The answer: no one, except by the grace of God that works in him and in all the servants to make souls know Christ and draw them to faith.

2.10.0.en: Paul describes the qualities of the true servant, giving himself as an example. These qualities are:

2.10.1.en: 1- Frankness and the absence of deceit or trickery in proclaiming Christ the Savior; he neither adds nor changes anything, as the heretics do.

2.10.2.en: 2- He preaches sincerely with all his strength to win souls.

2.10.3.en: 3- He prays and asks for God's help, because the power of preaching is by God's grace and power ("of God in Christ").

2.10.4.en: 4- He feels that he is in the presence of God as he speaks, so he is at ease, and also in reverence, during his ministry ("before God").

2.10.5.en: May we thank God before every work and after it, because everything is accomplished by His power. In this way we are saved from pride or faint-heartedness, and are not troubled by the scarcity or abundance of fruit, but remain steadfast in our service and our works and feel the presence of God more in our life.

2.10.6.en: A comparison between the Law and the New Testament
